name: sandbox
description: Run a shell command under OS-level confinement, and say which backend (if any) actually confined it.
author: Adaptive Agent Harness

tools.name: sandbox_run
tools.description: Run a command under an OS-level sandbox. Detects which confinement backends this machine actually supports, runs the command under the best one, and reports which backend was used -- including saying plainly when no confinement was available.

command.description: The command as an argv list, e.g. ["pytest", "-q"]. Prefer this: an argv list is never passed through a shell, so nothing in it is expanded, globbed or word-split.

backend.description: Which backend to use: landlock, bubblewrap, seatbelt, container, none, or "auto" to pick the best available. Defaults to auto. A name this plugin does not implement is refused rather than silently replaced.

timeout.description: Seconds before the process group is killed. Defaults to 120, maximum 300.

workspace.description: The directory the backends confine writes to. Defaults to the current working directory. Refused if it is the filesystem root, where confinement would be meaningless.
